standard_metadata.title: Avionics Software Requirement Verification Checklist & Quality Standard
standard_metadata.domain: Critical Embedded & Avionics Systems (Tailored IV&V Baseline)

mandatory_sections.name: Scope and System Overview
mandatory_sections.description: High-level description of the system, operational scope, and subsystem boundaries.

mandatory_sections.name: Functional Requirements
mandatory_sections.description: Deterministic functional requirements specifying software actions, transformations, and control logic.

mandatory_sections.name: Interface Requirements
mandatory_sections.description: Hardware, protocol, bus, or inter-process communication interfaces and data formats.

mandatory_sections.name: Safety and Failure Handling
mandatory_sections.description: Fault detection, exception handling, containment modes, and fail-safe recovery procedures.

requirement_rules.description: Every requirement statement must begin with or contain a unique alphanumeric tracking identifier (e.g., REQ-XXX-000).

Requirements must state quantitative, testable metrics and bounds rather than vague, subjective qualitative adjectives such as 'quickly', 'fast', 'easy', 'user-friendly', 'sufficient', 'approximately', 'optimal', or 'modern'.

Requirements must enforce binding obligation using definitive modal auxiliary verbs ('shall' or 'must'). Non-binding modals such as 'should', 'may', 'could', 'might', or 'will' must not be used for functional specifications.

Each requirement must describe a single discrete testable obligation. Statements should avoid bundling multiple independent functions using multi-clause conjunctions ('and also', 'additionally', 'as well as').
Critical inputs, sensor feeds, or bus telemetry processing requirements should specify condition-action response for corrupted, missing, or out-of-bound data.
